chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Sinan, from Hudhayfa ibn Mansur, from Mu'adh ibn Kathir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The month of Ramadan is thirty days, not deficient, by Allah, ever!

key_terms.أَبَداً: ever/always — temporal absolute, making the ruling universal
key_terms.ثَلَاثُونَ يَوْماً: thirty days — the fixed count asserted by the Imam
key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: The Month of Ramadan — the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, obligatory fasting month
key_terms.لَا يَنْقُصُ: not deficient/not reduced — the Imam's negation of any shortening
key_terms.وَاللَّهِ: by Allah — a solemn oath reinforcing the certainty of the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is the month of Ramadan always 30 days according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) makes a categorical assertion with a divine oath that the month of Ramadan always consists of exactly thirty days and never falls short. This ruling addresses a disputed question in early Islamic jurisprudence regarding whether Ramadan can be 29 days (crescent moon sighting dependent) or is fixed at 30. The Imam's insistence — reinforced by the solemn oath 'by Allah, ever!' — indicates a fixed-count position that diverges from the lunar sighting school, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential tradition that protects the integrity of the fasting month.
